headline: Recommended approval of UCH-TIF tax increment zone for Assembly Square and East Somerville, and of amended zoning rules for homeless shelters.
summary: The committee discussed a proposed Urban Center Housing Tax Increment Financing district covering parts of East Somerville and Assembly Square. Planning staff said the action only opens the door for negotiations and does not require use of the tool. The committee also recommended, as amended, a zoning change that requires a special permit for homeless shelters in Neighborhood Residence zones instead of allowing them by right.
decisions: Accepted the minutes of the May 21, 2026 meeting, 5-0.
Accepted the minutes of the June 18, 2026 meeting, 5-0.
Recommended approval of the Urban Center Housing Tax Increment Financing (UCH-TIF) Zone, Plan, and Form of Agreement for Assembly Square and East Somerville, 5-0.

Recommended approval, as amended, of the zoning amendment on homeless shelters, changing Homeless Shelter from permitted by right to special permit in the residential line of Table 3.1.16 and in the Neighborhood Residence column of Table 9.1.1, by a 5-0 roll call vote on the amendment.

## City of Somerville, Massachusetts City Council Land Use Committee Meeting Minutes

Thursday, September 3, 2026

6:30 PM

This meeting was held via Zoom and was called to order by Chair Ewen-Campen at 6:34 pm and adjourned at 7:42 pm on a roll call vote of 5 in favor (Councilors Davis, Clingan, Sait, McLaughlin and Ewen-Campen), 0 opposed, and 0 absent.

Others present: Samantha Carr - Land Use Analyst, Katherine Wiese - Economic Development Planner, Fiona DiMartino - Planning Division Deputy Director and Delaney Fisher-Cassiol - Clerk of Committees

Roll Call

- Present: Ward Six City Councilor Lance L. Davis, Ward Four City
- Councilor Jesse Clingan, Ward Five City Councilor Naima
- Sait, Ward One City Councilor Matthew McLaughlin and
- Ward Three City Councilor Ben Ewen-Campen

1. Committee

Approval of the Minutes of the Land Use Committee Meeting of May 21, Minutes

2026.

(ID # 26-0942 )

- RESULT: ACCEPTED

2. Committee

Approval of the Minutes of the Land Use Committee Meeting of June 18, Minutes

2026.

(ID # 26-1147 )

- RESULT: ACCEPTED
- AYE:

- Ward Six City Councilor Davis, Ward Four City Councilor
- Clingan, Ward Five City Councilor Sait, Ward One City
- Councilor McLaughlin and Ward Three City Councilor
- Ewen-Campen

3. Mayor's Request Requesting approval of the Urban Center Housing Tax Increment Financing

(ID # 26-0746 ) (UCH-TIF) Zone, Plan, and Form of Agreement for Assembly Square and East Somerville.

- Economic Development Planner Katherine Wiese explained that creating
- this proposed district, covering parts of East Somerville and Assembly
- Square, allows projects to request Urban Center Housing Tax Increment

Financing (UCHTIF). Planner Wiese emphasized that this authorizes the district's creation, serving as an alternative to encourage development while

preserving affordable housing without resorting to unsupported cuts to inclusionary housing requirements during a period of low housing starts. In

- response to a request for clarification from Councilor Clingan, Planner

Wiese confirmed the action only opens the door for negotiations rather than mandating tool usage.

- Councilor Clingan noted the designation could effectively incentivize

construction. Councilor McLaughlin highlighted the presence of abandoned businesses in East Somerville, expressing strong support for neighborhood

- revitalization efforts that maintain inclusionary housing requirements.

- RESULT: RECOMMENDED TO BE APPROVED
- AYE:

- Ward Six City Councilor Davis, Ward Four City Councilor
- Clingan, Ward Five City Councilor Sait, Ward One City
- Councilor McLaughlin and Ward Three City Councilor
- Ewen-Campen

4. Zoning Ordinance By Councilor Davis, Councilor Ewen-Campen, Councilor Clingan, (ID # 26-0835 ) Councilor Link, Councilor Mbah, Councilor Hardt, Councilor Sait and Councilor Wheeler

Proposing an amendment to Section 2.1.1 of the Zoning Ordinance regarding Homeless Shelters.

- Councilor Davis introduced this item and noted that the Council previously

discussed opening a homeless shelter in Ward 6 and explained that the intent of this item is to resolve confusion around the zoning ordinances and establish a clearer process to allow for more shelter options citywide. Chair

Ewen-Campen noted that the Planning Board issued a positive recommendation on the item and Land Use Analyst Samantha Carr reviewed

the document Land Use - 2026-09-03 Homeless Shelter Provisions Research

(with 26-0835).

Councilor Davis explained that while his initial draft included the Neighborhood Residence district to invite discussion, Analyst Carr's

research highlighted the need for a more nuanced approach. He suggested requiring a special permit in Neighborhood Residence zones for homeless

- shelters and by right with a required neighborhood meeting in Urban

Residence and commercial zones to lift development barriers. He added that the City Council could later pursue a separate amendment to create specific

definitions that would allow smaller-scale uses, such as family stabilization and homeless youth shelters, in neighborhood residential areas.

- Chair Ewen-Campen mentioned the Ward 3 warming center, located in a

Neighborhood Residence zone, noting it has brought both positives and challenges that underscore the importance of a transparent public process

- and careful deliberation during special permit reviews. In response to

Councilor Clingan’s question about if the proposal applies to drop-in style shelters, Councilor Davis clarified that essentially it does, noting that while certain shelter uses are already allowed, this proposal would permit defined

homeless shelters either by right or via special permit depending on the zone. Councilor Sait expressed support for homeless shelters in these areas

- and asked how special permit conditions and nuances would be handled.

- Planning Division Deputy Director Fiona DiMartino confirmed that special

permits for shelters would follow standard review procedures, allowing specific restrictions to be placed on a permit on a case-by-case basis.

- Councilor Clingan noted that the special permit process provides helpful
- flexibility depending on the specific use of the shelter.

Councilor Davis moved to amend Table 3.1.16 (Permitted Uses) by changing the designation for "Homeless Shelter" in the residential line from "P" (Permitted By Right) to "SP" (Special Permit) and and Table 9.1.1 (Permitted Uses) by changing the designation for "Homeless Shelter" in the Neighborhood Residence (NR) column from "P" (Permitted By Right) to "SP" (Special Permit). The motion was approved on a roll call vote of 5 in favor (Councilors Davis, Clingan, Sait, McLaughlin and Ewen-Campen), 0 opposed, and 0 absent. RESULT: RECOMMENDED TO BE APPROVED AS

AMENDED
